knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)

*Written 2026-11-26.* These notes are for whoever takes over the project.
They describe how things are set up and how to work on them. For what has
been found so far, and why, read the [lab notebook](lab-notebook.html),
starting with its status table.

## 1. Where things stand

**Aim.** Estimate vaccine effectiveness as a function of time since
vaccination, VE(t), using a Poisson approximation to a Cox model in which
the baseline hazard is driven by an age-structured force of infection (FoI).
The project started as Group D at the Lorentz Center workshop (June 2026).

**What works.**

- The full pipeline, from raw vaccination and case records to a fitted
  VE(t) curve, is in the package, tested, and documented on the
  [website](https://kylieainslie.github.io/surviver/).
- On simulated data with a known VE(t), the model recovers the curve and
  distinguishes waning from no waning (lab notebook entry 7).

**Known limitations** (details in the lab notebook):

- The estimate lags the truth by about a week, because time since
  vaccination is measured to the report date, not the infection date
  (entry 7).
- Late VE (90+ days) is underestimated in the waning scenario. About half of
  this comes from calendar time being confounded with time since
  vaccination (entry 9).
- In the current simulations the FoI adds no precision, because vaccination
  is random with respect to exposure (entry 10).
- HERMES resets the immunity of recovered people when it vaccinates them
  (entry 11).

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This package: code, data, Stan models, tests, website, lab notebook | GitHub [`kylieainslie/surviver`](https://github.com/kylieainslie/surviver) (public, branch `main`) |
| HERMES simulator with the waning-VE extension | GitHub [`kylieainslie/ibm_hermes`](https://github.com/kylieainslie/ibm_hermes/tree/waning-vaccine-effectiveness), branch **`waning-vaccine-effectiveness`**. A fork of `lwillem/ibm_hermes` (Lander Willem); our changes are not upstream |
| Workshop record: original scripts, case-study data (200,000 people), the first Group D vignettes | GitHub [`kylieainslie/lorentz_center_workshop`](https://github.com/kylieainslie/lorentz_center_workshop), branch `group-D`, `analysis/group-D/` and `data/`. Kept as a historical record; not developed further |

**Package layout.**

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `R/prepare.R` | Data preparation: `ve_population()`, `daily_incidence()`, `daily_prevalence()`, `counting_process()`, `expand_person_days()`, … |
| `R/foi.R` | `force_of_infection()`, `age_group_sizes()` |
| `R/contact_hermes.R` | `contact_matrix_hermes()` |

| `inst/stan/` | `ve_noncentered.stan` (default) and `ve_centered.stan` |

| `tests/testthat/` | Unit tests (no Stan fitting, so they run without CmdStan) |

| `.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml` | Builds and deploys the website |

## 3. Setting up

```{r}
# 1. Clone both repositories (shell):
#    git clone https://github.com/kylieainslie/surviver.git
#    git clone -b waning-vaccine-effectiveness https://github.com/kylieainslie/ibm_hermes.git

# 2. R packages (from the surviver folder)
install.packages(c("devtools", "pak"))
pak::local_install_dev_deps()       # Imports + Suggests, incl. cmdstanr from GitHub

# 3. CmdStan, for fitting
cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()

# 4. Tell surviver where HERMES is, if not at ~/Documents/ibm_hermes.
#    Add to ~/.Renviron:   HERMES_PATH=/path/to/ibm_hermes

# 5. Check everything works
devtools::test()
devtools::check()
```

Versions used so far: R 4.5.2, CmdStan 2.39.0. `fit_ve()` caches the
compiled Stan model in `tools::R_user_dir("surviver", "cache")`; delete that
folder if a model seems stale after editing a `.stan` file.

HERMES itself is not an R package. Its scripts `source()` each other with
paths relative to the repository root, so always load it from that folder:

```{r}
hermes <- new.env()
withr::with_dir(Sys.getenv("HERMES_PATH", "~/Documents/ibm_hermes"), {
  sys.source("lib/ibm_core.R", envir = hermes)
  sys.source("lib/ibm_waning_scenario.R", envir = hermes)
})
```

## 4. Working conventions

- **Lab notebook.** Every check or validation run gets a dated entry in
  `vignettes/articles/lab-notebook.Rmd` with question, method, results as
  observed, conclusion, and next step, plus a script in `dev/checks/`. Save
  figures to `vignettes/articles/figures/` with the same date prefix. Never
  edit past results; add a new entry or a dated note. Update the status
  table and timeline at the top.
- **Check scripts** run from the package root, load the package with
  `devtools::load_all()`, and write outputs to `$SURVIVER_CHECKS_OUT`
  (default: a temporary folder).
- **Website.** Pushing to `main` rebuilds it. To preview locally:
  `pkgdown::build_site()` and open `docs/index.html` (`docs/` is
  git-ignored).
- **Changes to HERMES** go on the `waning-vaccine-effectiveness` branch of
  the fork. Commit before regenerating data, because each dataset records
  the HERMES commit it came from, and the data script warns if HERMES has
  uncommitted changes.

## 5. Regenerating the simulated datasets

The package datasets `ve_sim_waning` and `ve_sim_no_waning` come from
`data-raw/ve_test_scenarios.R`:

```{r}
# from the surviver folder
source("data-raw/ve_test_scenarios.R")   # about 20 s per scenario
devtools::document()
devtools::test()                         # tests/testthat/test-data.R checks structure
```

The script loads HERMES, calls `simulate_waning_scenario()` once with
`ve_floor = 0.1` and once with `ve_floor = 0.8`, drops HERMES-only columns,
stores the HERMES commit in `hermes_commit`, and saves with
`usethis::use_data()`.

**Reproducibility.** Every random step in the scenario is seeded from
`rng_seed` (default 2026), including reporting. The current datasets were
made with HERMES commit `6c9ab73`; later commits on the branch reproduce them
exactly. If a regenerated dataset changes, record that in the lab notebook,
because earlier entries' numbers refer to the old data.

**Getting what the datasets leave out.** The exported tables only contain
what an analyst would see. HERMES keeps the full state of every person (true
infection time, symptom onset, death, …). Run with a known `output_dir` and
read the final snapshot:

```{r}
sc  <- hermes$simulate_waning_scenario(ve_floor = 0.1, output_dir = "out/waning")
full <- readRDS("out/waning/pop_data_intervention16.rds")   # 16 = n_chunks
full$ind_id <- rownames(full)
# columns include time_of_infection, time_of_symptom_onset, health,
# time_of_vaccination, time_of_death, infector_id, ...
```

Snapshots after each vaccination round are `pop_data_intervention1.rds` …
`pop_data_interventionN.rds`. Lab notebook entries 8 and 11 use these.

## 6. Adapting the simulations

### Changing scenario settings

`simulate_waning_scenario()` (HERMES `lib/ibm_waning_scenario.R`) takes:

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ve_floor` | 0.1 | Long-run VE after waning; set equal to `vaccine_effectiveness` for no waning |
| `vaccine_effectiveness` | 0.8 | Peak VE |
| `ve_ramp_days` | 14 | Days to reach peak VE |
| `ve_half_life` | 45 | Half-life of the waning, in days |
| `pop_size` | 10,000 | Population size (runtime grows with it; 100,000 has not been timed) |
| `transmission_prob` | 0.02 | Per-contact transmission probability. Chosen so the epidemic lasts the whole study; see lab notebook entry 2 before changing it |
| `num_infected_seeds` | 10 | Initial infections |
| `initial_days` | 20 | Days before vaccination starts |
| `n_chunks`, `chunk_days` | 16, 10 | Number and length of vaccination rounds; study length is `initial_days + n_chunks * chunk_days` |
| `chunk_coverage` | 0.03 | Share of the eligible population vaccinated per round |
| `rng_seed` | 2026 | Seed for all random steps |
| `output_dir` | temporary | Where HERMES writes its snapshots |

Other HERMES parameters (contact probabilities, natural history, reporting
delay) are set in `lib/ibm_parameters.R` (`get_default_parameters()`) and
`lib/ibm_delay_parameters.R`. Changing those defaults affects **every**
HERMES scenario, so prefer setting them inside the scenario function.

### Using a new scenario without adding it to the package

```{r}
sc <- hermes$simulate_waning_scenario(ve_floor = 0.3, ve_half_life = 90)
sim <- list(
  demographic = sc$demographic_data,
  vaccination = sc$vaccination_data,
  incidence   = sc$incidence_data_reduced,
  params      = sc$params,
  study_end   = sc$study_end
)
pop <- ve_population(sim)        # then the usual pipeline (see README)
truth <- true_ve(1:160, sim$params)
```

Alternatively, `hermes$export_waning_scenario(sc, "some/folder")` writes the
four `.rds` files, and `ve_population("some/folder")` reads them.

### Adding a new scenario to the package

1. Add a call in `data-raw/ve_test_scenarios.R` (or a new `data-raw/`
   script) and include it in `usethis::use_data()`.
2. Document it in `R/data.R` and run `devtools::document()`.
3. Extend `tests/testthat/test-data.R`.
4. Add a lab-notebook entry describing it, like entry 5.

### Replicate simulations

Use different `rng_seed` values. Each seed changes the synthetic population
as well as the epidemic, and epidemic size varies a lot between seeds (seed
7 gave 1,156 reported cases against 1,566 for seed 2026), so record the
number of cases among vaccinated people per replicate. A sketch:

```{r}
run_one <- function(seed, ve_floor) {
  sc  <- hermes$simulate_waning_scenario(ve_floor = ve_floor, rng_seed = seed)
  sim <- list(demographic = sc$demographic_data, vaccination = sc$vaccination_data,
              incidence = sc$incidence_data_reduced, params = sc$params,
              study_end = sc$study_end)
  pop  <- ve_population(sim)
  prev <- daily_prevalence(daily_incidence(pop))
  foi  <- force_of_infection(prev, age_group_sizes(pop))
  sd   <- make_stan_data(expand_person_days(counting_process(pop)), foi)
  ve   <- extract_ve(fit_ve(sd, seed = seed, refresh = 0, show_messages = FALSE))
  ve$truth <- true_ve(ve$days_since_vax, sim$params)
  ve$seed  <- seed
  ve
}
# about 20 s simulation + 40 s fit per replicate; parallelise over seeds
# (e.g. with the future/furrr packages, one chain per core).
```

Summarise bias (median − truth), coverage of the 90% interval and interval
width by range of days since vaccination. The piecewise GLM in
`dev/checks/2026-11-25_03_calendar_time.R` takes seconds and is a useful
quick screen before running Stan on every replicate.

### Changing how HERMES vaccinates

Vaccination happens at the start of each `rerun_ibm()` call in
`lib/ibm_core.R` (look for `is_eligible`):

```{r}
is_eligible <- which(pop_data$health != states$V & pop_data$health != states$D)
id_vaccinated <- sample(is_eligible, round(length(is_eligible) * params$vaccine_coverage, 0))
pop_data$health[id_vaccinated] <- states$V
pop_data$time_of_vaccination[id_vaccinated] <- nprev_days
```

- **Stop resetting immunity in recovered people** (lab notebook entry 11):
  for people in state `R`, record `time_of_vaccination` but leave `health`
  as `R`. Decide whether infectious people (`I`) should be vaccinated at
  all.
- **Targeted vaccination** (e.g. oldest first): replace `sample()` with a
  selection that prioritises by `pop_data$age`. Add a new parameter (e.g.
  `vaccine_priority = NULL`) and keep the current random selection when it
  is `NULL`, so other scenarios are unchanged.

Both changes alter the simulated data, so regenerate the datasets and add a
lab-notebook entry.

## 7. Where to go next

In rough order of priority. The lab notebook explains the reasons.

1. **Let transmission vary over calendar time in the model.** Add a random
   walk on `log_beta` over calendar weeks (or days) to a new Stan model in
   `inst/stan/`, keeping the FoI offset. `make_stan_data()` already keeps
   `day` in its cells; pass a week index to Stan. Add the model name to
   `ve_stan_file()` and `fit_ve()`. Expected to remove the calendar-time
   part of the late underestimate (entry 9).
2. **Decide on vaccination of recovered people** in HERMES (entry 11) and,
   if changing it, regenerate the datasets.
3. **Replicate simulations** (above) to measure bias and coverage properly.
   Only then judge whether a frailty term is needed.
4. **Targeted-vaccination scenario**, to test the project's premise that the
   FoI improves VE estimation when exposure differs between vaccinated and
   unvaccinated people (entry 10).
5. **Frailty**, if bias remains after 1–3. Note the model works on
   aggregated cells, so an individual random effect is not possible
   directly; a gamma frailty integrated out analytically (hazard divided by
   1 + θ × cumulative hazard) can work at cell level.
6. **Delays between infection and reporting** (entry 7). Options range from
   measuring time since vaccination to an estimated infection date to
   treating infection time as latent.
7. **Apply to the workshop case study** (`data/` in the workshop repo, read
   with `ve_population("path/to/data")`). Decide the value of `theta` first
   (entry 1 records the inconsistency).

## 8. Loose ends

- **HERMES reporting seed.** `get_default_delay_parameters()` has no
  `rng_seed`, so reporting is unseeded in every HERMES run outside our
  scenario function (lab notebook entry 4). Worth reporting to Lander
  Willem (`lwillem/ibm_hermes`).
- **HERMES default parameters.** Our branch changed package-wide defaults
  (waning VE, hospitalisation, mortality; entry 2). Revert these to the
  originals before proposing the branch upstream, and set them inside the
  scenario function instead.
- **Outdated documents.** `ibm_hermes/doc/vaccine_waning_vignette.Rmd`
  still describes a 100,000-person scenario and old output paths. The
  workshop repo's `data/ve_test_scenarios/` and its simulated-data vignette
  predate the reproducibility fix (entry 4); the package versions are the
  reference.
- **Stan prior on the first day.** Both models put
  \(\gamma(1) \sim N(-1, 1)\), i.e. a prior centred on about 63% VE on
  the first day after vaccination. In the simulations VE starts at 0, so a
  prior centred at 0 may be more sensible. Not yet tested.
- **POLYMOD lookup.** `socialmixr` warns that the automatic population
  lookup used in `data-raw/polymod_nl.R` is deprecated. The saved matrix is
  unaffected, but the script will need `survey_pop` in future versions.
- **Citation.** The waning-VE meta-analysis cited as "Ferdinands et al.
  2018, *J Infect Dis* 217:731" may be by Young et al.; check before
  publishing.
- **Continuous integration.** Only the website is built on GitHub.
  Consider adding `usethis::use_github_action("check-standard")` so tests
  run on every push.
